html:
The Chachi, once called the Cayapa, are an Indigenous people of the forested rivers of Esmeraldas province in north-west Ecuador, along the Cayapas, Onzole and Santiago rivers. They speak Cha'palaa, a language of the Barbacoan family, related to the languages of the Tsáchila and the Awá.

Their own traditions say they once lived in the Andean highlands near Ibarra and moved down to the coastal lowlands around the time of the Inca or Spanish conquest. They live in stilt houses on the riverbanks, fish, hunt and grow plantains, and are known for their canoes and basketry. Their neighbours include Afro-Ecuadorian communities descended from Africans who escaped slavery and settled Esmeraldas from the 1500s.
